envelope.text: CALLER-PLACED: fills `out` and returns `Result`, where upstream returns a

why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` IS an `rclcpp::Node`, so this is `rclcpp::Node::create_subscription`, inherited, with `cpp:Node::create_subscription`'s contract. The extractor records only the members a class declares, so this key correlates as upstream-only even though the name resolves.

Before phase-482 W4: RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-23 (phase-444 ledger re-read), gap -> declined, AND THE ROW'S TWO FIELDS HAD CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER: `disposition` said `absent` while the reason's headline announced REFUSE-LOUD. MEASURED 2026-09-23, `absent` is the true one and the headline is now the field. `nros::LifecycleNode` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:340`) declares no `create_publisher` and no `create_subscription`, deleted or otherwise — the class's only `= delete` is its copy pair (`:355-356`) and it holds no `static_assert` refusal. A porting user gets `undeclared identifier`.

THIS ROW IS PURELY ABOUT THE RECEIVER, and the reason it carried until 2026-09-21 was a verbatim COPY of the publisher's, which made it wrong twice over: it argued about sends being dropped while inactive, and upstream's `LifecycleNode::create_subscription` returns an ORDINARY subscription — `rclcpp_lifecycle` has no `LifecycleSubscription` at all. Nothing here is about gating a publisher.

WHY `declined` AND NOT `gap`: the capability REP-2002 is about SHIPS, and what upstream's verb needs is a RECEIVER we deliberately do not have. `nros::LifecyclePublisher<M>` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:1078`) drops `publish()` while the node is not Active, `SimpleManagedEntity` (`:321`) carries the `on_activate`/`on_deactivate` pair, and `LifecycleNode::add_managed_entity` (`:645`) runs every registered entity's hook on a successful transition (`:977`, `:982`). Our `LifecycleNode` is a MIXIN over the state machine, not a node, so it is the `rclcpp::Node` that creates entities and upstream's two-argument member has nothing to be a member of. The header states exactly that and shows the two-line replacement (`:1065-1078`), which is what `bind(Node&)` costs.

THE BUILD-LIST ITEM SURVIVES THE RE-VERDICT, as a DISPOSITION item: one `= delete` or dependent `static_assert` on `nros::LifecycleNode` carrying `node.create_publisher(pub_.publisher(), "/topic"); lifecycle_node.add_managed_entity(&pub_);` moves this row from `absent` to `refuse-loud`. It does not change the verdict — a decline stays a decline whether or not it is announced — and it is worth having because this is how every rclcpp_lifecycle demo is written and `no member named 'create_publisher'` teaches nothing. ONE diagnostic covers the concept: `create_publisher`, `create_subscription`, and the `create_client`/`create_service` siblings this shard's neighbours already carry as `declined`/`absent`.

WHAT THE 2026-09-21 PASS GOT RIGHT, AND WHAT IT LEFT. It was right that the original reason — "We have lifecycle state and no entity that observes it; a deactivated node's publishers keep publishing" — is FALSE, phase-417 W4.f having shipped that entity; that paragraph is now DELETED rather than left standing above its own refutation. It also recorded, correctly, that `--check --require-disposition` had relabelled its `refuse-loud` to `absent` in the same pass that wrote it, because a refusal is a declaration and no symbol is declared. Every line number it cited has since drifted and is re-measured above: `LifecyclePublisher` :999 -> :1078, `SimpleManagedEntity` :265 -> :321, `add_managed_entity` :577 -> :645, the mixin note :1006-1012 -> :1065-1078.
